reader_summary.overview: Hi, and welcome to the A16Z podcast. I'm Hannah, and in this episode we talk all about the remarkable story of one American family, the Galvins, Mimi, Don, their 10 sons. Robert Colker, author of the book and previous author of Lost Girls, writes, They lived through the eras of institutionalization and shock therapy.

key_points.text: I'm Hannah, and in this episode we talk all about the remarkable story of one American family, the Galvins, Mimi, Don, their 10 sons.
key_points.evidence_quote: I'm Hannah, and in this episode we talk all about the remarkable story of one American family, the Galvins, Mimi, Don, their 10 sons, and two girls, out of whom six sons were afflicted with schizophrenia, following them from the 1950s to today.

key_points.text: Robert Colker, author of the book and previous author of Lost Girls, writes, They lived through the eras of institutionalization and shock therapy.
key_points.evidence_quote: Robert Colker, author of the book and previous author of Lost Girls, writes, They lived through the eras of institutionalization and shock therapy, the debates between psychotherapy versus medication, the needle in a haystack search for genetic markers for the disease, and the profound disagreements about the cause and origin of the illness itself.

key_points.text: And because of that, this story is really more than just a portrait of one family.
key_points.evidence_quote: And because of that, this story is really more than just a portrait of one family.

key_points.text: It's a portrait of how we have struggled to understand this mental illness, the biology of it, the drivers, the behaviors and pathology.
key_points.evidence_quote: It's a portrait of how we have struggled to understand this mental illness, the biology of it, the drivers, the behaviors and pathology, the genomics of it, and of course the search for treatments that might help.
